title: Weak Evidence Base for Science Reform (Meta-Science Gap)
bottleneck: Meta-science rarely has randomized trials of funding reforms; when trials exist they are small, one-off, and measure unclear endpoints like citations rather than real discovery. Proposed reforms therefore rest on theory and anecdote, and opponents can dismiss every pilot as non-generalizable. Endpoints like citations correlate weakly with genuine breakthroughs, making even well-designed trials hard to interpret.
why_it_blocks: Reform without evidence is guesswork, but the evidence is structurally hard to produce — a trap that protects the status quo. Reformers and defenders thus argue past each other, each citing selected cases.
current_state: The meta-science field is growing (RoRI, metascience conferences), but causal evidence on what funding designs work remains thin. Building better measures of scientific progress is itself a bottleneck for the field.

sources.title: Evidence and the Design and Reform of Scientific Institutions (Nintil)
